proposal: One exact, dated national establishment-class observation is recovered. It is a candidate for a standalone Japanese government detailed-industry series, not for comparison with CESA ecosystem estimates or CEDEC respondent demographics.

observations.reference_date: 2012 (survey year; confirm exact enumeration date in downloaded table metadata before presentation)
observations.definition: National workers in establishments classified as 3914 Game software industry: establishments creating game software, including component programs, for home-TV game machines, portable electronic game machines and PCs, and conducting related research, analysis or advice. The classification excludes game-cassette and game-optical-disc manufacturing.
observations.methodology: Economic Census activity survey; official national establishment tabulation. The published table notes that establishment, worker and sales values cover establishments for which required items were obtained, and excludes management/support establishments from this establishment tabulation.
observations.scope_limits: Domestic establishment industry classification. It is not all employment at diversified game publishers or console-hardware companies, not a developer-occupation count, and not a contractor/FTE measure.
observations.source_locator: Results overview, p. 2 / Table I-1, row 3914 ゲームソフトウェア業: 246 establishments; 9,452 workers.
observations.assessment: primary official source; dated and exact; candidate series anchor only. Do not interpolate or combine with CESA values.

not_proposed.item: CESA Game Industry Report 2024/2025 workforce estimates
not_proposed.reason: Employment reference year and detailed reproducible method are not public; the 2025 core range includes console hardware and the broad estimate includes many related industries.
Voluntary online survey respondent demographics, not national workforce stocks.
Input-output-model induced employment associated with economic effects, explicitly not necessarily additional jobs.
